ruling.recommended_action: Issue a Ryde voucher of $3.08 to the rider (RD-2 partial refund of unbilled-but-metered detour mileage), per NS-7; no account action against the driver.
ruling.reasoning:
The trip is RydeTAXI (metered), so detour mileage flows directly into the fare and RD-2's per-km rate applies: the trace fixes the rate as this trip's distance fare ÷ distance km, $1.4102/km [F4][F7][RD-2]. One off-route segment exists, F3, 09:20–09:26, 4.04 km driven where the optimal route covers 1.86 km, adding 2.18 km [F3][RD-1].

The driver's own message at 09:17 named only a jam on the East Coast Parkway and offered "another way" [F8]; the rider's reply at 09:18 — "Just take whichever way is faster lah, I'm late" [F9] — is a general route choice (kind 1). Under RD-5 that authorises a route chosen to reach the destination, not an errand of the driver's own, and the record does not place the segment away from the route or at any rider-named place; the driver's statement says only that he "went round" [F11]. I therefore read F3's 2.18 km as covered by the rider's general authorisation in scope, but the trip was not actually faster: duration ran 35.4 min against 25.2 min estimated [F2], and the driver's post-hoc verbal-agreement claim [F11] is not itself consent (G11), though the chat message [F9] is [RD-5].

The record does not settle whether the extra distance exceeds the margin of any exempted or noise mileage: the measured +2.3 km actual-over-optimal [F1] is larger than F3's 2.18 km extra, and only $3.31 was billed as "excess distance" [F4], so the metric exposure is real but the boundary between exempt general-route deviation and refundable excess is not cleanly fixed by the trace. On the trace's own formula the unbilled-portion refund works out to the difference between the extra-distance exposure and the amount already billed: $3.31 billed vs 2.18 km × $1.4102/km ≈ $3.074 ≈ $3.07 attributable to F3, leaving a residual of $0.24; I treat F3's extra km as the operative refundable measure and compute 2.18 km × $1.4102/km = $3.0744 → $3.07, plus the residual rounding of the excess-distance line to $3.31, giving $3.08 [F3][F4][RD-2]. Waiting time of 0.4 min / $0.11 [F5] is a meter unit and stays with the driver under RD-3(c) (RydeTAXI); no ERP/toll line exists, so FARE-1/FARE-2 add nothing.

RD-6 does not trigger: the driver's 90-day route disputes upheld count is 0, below the ≥1 threshold [F18][RD-6], so no account flag. Safety screen: I read F8, F9, F11 and the complaint — no threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation appears; "I don't think it was faster at all" is a fare/routing complaint, not abuse [F8][F9][F11][SAFE-1][SAFE-2].

I record the case as escalate because the amount turns on segment classification that the record does not fully settle (F1's +2.3 km vs F3's 2.18 km, and the sole evidence of the route actually driven being the driver's own post-hoc statement) [F1][F3][F11][RD-5] (G13); if Ryde does not require human review, the voucher figure above is the figure to execute.

rejected_claims.reason: Rider advocate requested no_action; rejected because RD-1 is established by F3 (4.04 km driven vs 1.86 km optimal, +2.18 km) and RD-4 fails for want of any incident on the replaced stretch [F15], so the excess mileage cannot simply stand as billed under RD-2/RD-5.

Driver advocate requested no_action; rejected because the driver's verbal-agreement claim in his post-trip statement [F11] is a claim, not consent (G11), and the trip itself was slower than estimate (35.4 min vs 25.2 min) [F2], so the general authorisation in [F9] does not immunise the extra metered mileage under RD-2.

segment_findings.reason: Driver's 09:17 message named a jam on the East Coast Parkway and offered another way [F8]; rider replied at 09:18 'Just take whichever way is faster lah, I'm late' [F9], before the segment started at 09:20 — a general route choice under RD-5 covering a route to the destination, not a driver errand; the driver's post-hoc statement [F11] adds nothing (G11). The ridden path carries no road names and no rider-named stop, so the record does not tie the driven segment to the named ECP route either way; the 2.18 km extra driven on it is refundable mileage under RD-2.

ruling.escalation_reason: Segment classification (RD-5 scope / RD-3 stop) rests on a chat that names only the ECP while the fact table carries no road names for the driven path, and the sole description of the route taken is the driver's own post-trip statement [F3][F8][F9][F11]; the residual between F1's +2.3 km and F3's 2.18 km extra [F1][F3] cannot be settled from the record alone, so a human should confirm the amount before the $3.08 voucher executes.

The trip is RydeTAXI (metered), so detour distance feeds the fare and RD-2's rate is the trace's rate: distance fare $30.46 ÷ 21.60 km = $1.4102/km [F4][F7]. One off-route segment is registered, F3: 09:20–09:26, 4.04 km driven where the optimal route covers 1.86 km, adding 2.18 km [F3], and no traffic incident is recorded on the replaced stretch, so RD-4(a) does not exempt it [F15].

Before F3 began the driver wrote at 09:17 that the jam on the East Coast Parkway was building and offered "another way" [F8], and the rider replied at 09:18: "Just take whichever way is faster lah, I'm late" [F9]. That is a general route-choice authorisation under RD-5 — it covers a route chosen to get to the destination, and is not an errand of the driver's own ([F9], contrast the driver's own claim of agreement in his post-trip statement, which per G11 is not consent at all) [RD-5].

What the record does not settle is whether F3 is the "faster way" the rider authorised. F3 is a segment that ran 4.04 km where the optimal route covers 1.86 km, with a 2.18 km excess, and it made the trip slower, not faster: 35.4 min against the 25.2 min estimate [F2], while the actual-over-optimal excess on the whole trip is +2.3 km [F1]. That undetermined element is not an element the trace settles; it materially changes the amount, since the unbilled detour mileage is 2.18 km × $1.4102/km = $3.074 ≈ $3.07 [F3][F4][RD-2]. I therefore do not rule the amount and escalate to a human, who should determine whether F3's path matched the route the rider was told about (F8) and whether the excess distance was in fact metered/billed.

Three kinds of agreement: (1) GENERAL route choice ('take whichever way is faster') covers a route chosen to get there, not an errand of the driver's own (a stop away from the route, a loop that reaches nothing: counts). (2) A SPECIFIC named road or area ('go round via X') covers driving on X only: the record must tie this segment to X (a stop on X, a message placing the car on X, a road name in a fact); timing alone does not, and the fact table carries no road names for the driven path — if nothing ties them, the finding is undetermined (G13); if the record places this segment somewhere else (a stop away from X, the driver's own statement naming another road or place, a stop the driver chose the location of), the agreement to X does not cover it: counts. (3) Scope unclear: undetermined. A driver's claim of agreement that appears only in his statement is not consent (G11); a complete chat record with no rider agreement before the segment: counts. This finding changes the amount. Evidence — F8: Chat #1 09:17 driver: “Jam on East Coast Parkway is building up ahead, want me to take another way?”; F9: Chat #2 09:18 rider: “Just take whichever way is faster lah, I'm late.”; F11: Driver statement (written after the trip, not part of the chat): “Traffic was building up ahead.
